newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thai plans 4th Paris freighter/rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Thai plans 4th Paris freighter/rate hike.

text.p: Thai Airways is adding an extra Boeing 747 freighter on its Paris route and considering raising cargo rates from the end of October, a Paris/CDG-based Thai cargo official told Reuters.
The additional weekly Boeing 747 freighter between Paris and Bangkok would be on Mondays, effective end-October.
The extra flight is in response to demand for more east and westbound space and Thai's Paris cargo office was also pushing for "very moderate" rates increases in October, the official added.

"The monetary climate, namely the strong dollar and weak Thai currency, as well as fierce competition from other carriers and the prospect of extra capacity will all be determining factors in this decision."
Thai already runs three weekly Paris-Bangkok 747F services, two of which are operated in conjunction with Air France.
Both Thai and Air France had indicated their willingness to operate two of the four weekly freighter frequencies on the route although this had yet to be officially confirmed, the official said.
Thai's Paris freighters also carries freight to and from the Benelux, Spain, the UK and Switzerland.
The Thai carrier also transports ex-Paris freight aboard a daily passenger service to Bangkok.

Figures from the Paris airport authority showed imports from Bangkok totalled 6,737 tonnes in the first six months of 1997, an increase of 33.6 percent on the same period last year while exports rose by 5.6 percent to 3,876 tonnes.
